title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Drafting Plate. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Drafting Plate
options.thesis: The portfolio reads as one engineering drawing: identity is the title block, work is the plate detail.
options.viewport: A full-bleed sheet whose title block holds Spencer Hodson, AI Native Software Engineer, one line of notes, stamped nav, and an approve-stamp contact action.
options.risk: Reads as engineer cosplay if the plate grammar stays decorative instead of structural.

raised.raise: Binary Plate Commitment — ink and sheet only; no grey mush, one drafting cyan for active marks.
State-as-Mark — featured work and current role use tape-flag / revision marks, never soft colored badges.
Lockup Scale Survival — Spencer Hodson must still read when stamped down to the nav cell.
Depth-as-Scroll — title block owns the first viewport; experience and projects deepen as plate details below.

options.label: Agent Session Log
options.thesis: Hiring proof is a designed session log: identity as the run header, projects as turns.
options.viewport: A session header with Spencer Hodson / AI Native Software Engineer, then turn cards that open into Work and Projects.
options.risk: Also the direction most AI-engineer portfolios land on when they try to look native.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Career objects plotted by magnitude on a night chart; projects are stars, experience is constellation lines.
options.viewport: Deep navy plate with Spencer Hodson as the labeled object under a red ring, projects as magnitude-scaled dots.
options.case: Holds audience identification with diagram culture; loses product clarity for a three-page hiring scan.
options.risk: Hiring managers may enjoy the chart and still not know what to do.

options.label: Data Sublime
options.thesis: Identity and work dissolve into a pure black-and-white barcode lattice.
options.viewport: A full-bleed barcode field with name recoverable only by sampling a column.
options.case: Loses both axes: recruiters do not identify with strobing data art, and the offer disappears.
options.kept: Absolute binary contrast and tabular density courage.
options.risk: Beautiful and unusable for a hiring decision.

options.label: Cutting Bench
options.thesis: Career frames string on a perforated rail; the stop is a folded tape flag.
options.viewport: An orange grain strip of punched frames for Home, Experience, and Projects.
options.case: Loses audience identification: editors, not engineers.
options.kept: State-as-mark discipline and rank by cell count.

options.label: Moon-Shadow Bazaar
options.thesis: Projects trade as shadows tagged with origin tickets.
options.viewport: A lane of stalls where each project is a tagged shadow for sale.
options.case: Loses both axes: surreal commerce cannot carry hiring proof.
options.kept: Every work item keeps an origin ticket.
options.risk: Fantasy where a decision is needed.

options.label: Mesophotic Dive
options.thesis: Scroll is a descent; contact is the ascent plan.
options.viewport: A vertical depth axis with name at the surface and work in the dark.
options.case: Loses both axes: ocean drama is not this product's world.

options.label: Deck Wall
options.thesis: Projects hang as full-bleed decks you pull and flip.
options.viewport: A screaming rack of project decks under shop light.
options.case: Loses product clarity for full-time hiring trust.
options.risk: Shop energy where a resume is being read.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished dark developer portfolio: name, role, project cards, contact.
canonCard.viewport: Centered identity hero over a three-up project grid and a contact strip.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other engineer site by design.
